notes: Brackets: PDF page 75 prints Schedule X (single or married/RDP filing separately), Schedule Y (married/RDP filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse/RDP) and Schedule Z (head of household), nine rates from 1% to 12.3%, for Form 540 line 19 taxable income over 100,000. married_separate is Schedule X (one schedule printed for both statuses); qualifying surviving spouse uses Schedule Y (the schema has no list for it). The printed tax at each band start agrees with the rates (Schedule X: 110.79 at 11,079 ... 72,219.84 at 742,953; Schedule Y 144,439.65 at 1,485,906; Schedule Z 97,472.91 at 1,010,417).

Tax Table: taxable income of 100,000 or less uses the Tax Table on PDF pages 69 to 73 ($100 rows). It is not recorded; rows checked against the schedules agree to the dollar at the row midpoint: 30,051-30,150: 568 / 380 / 380; 60,051-60,150: 2,192 / 1,132 / 1,132; 99,951-100,000: 5,736 / 3,068 / 3,708 (status 1 or 3 / 2 or 5 / 4). The schedules start at 0, so the bracket list covers all incomes.

Surtax: the Behavioral Health Services Tax (PDF page 16, Form 540 line 62; PDF page 5 says the Mental Health Services Tax is renamed from 2025) is 1% of Form 540 line 19 taxable income over 1,000,000, one threshold printed for every filing status. It is added on line 62, after the exemption and other credits (line 32 to 48).

Starting point: Form 540 line 13 is federal AGI; Schedule CA (540) subtractions (line 14) and additions (line 16) give California AGI (line 17); line 18 subtracts the larger of California itemized deductions or the standard deduction; line 19 is taxable income. The booklet says California itemized deductions may be limited based on federal AGI (PDF page 13; Schedule CA Part II line 29 uses the same 252,203 / 378,310 / 504,411 amounts, PDF page 52).

Exemptions are credits against tax, not deductions from income (PDF page 14: 'Exemption credits reduce your tax'; Form 540 line 11 total goes to line 32, subtracted from the line 31 tax, line 33 not below zero). They are recorded as credit reliefs (form credit, credit_amount, credit_basis tax, covers all_income), not in base.deductions, so a consumer subtracts them from tax. credit_basis 'tax' here means the credit is taken off the tax; it is a fixed amount, not a share of it (no credit_rate).

Exemption credit amounts: Form 540 PDF page 39 prints 'X $153' on lines 7 (personal), 8 (blind) and 9 (senior) and 'X $475' on line 10 (each dependent). Personal: 1 box for filing status 1, 3 or 4 (single, married/RDP filing separately, head of household), 2 for status 2 or 5 (married/RDP filing jointly, qualifying surviving spouse/RDP); a qualifying surviving spouse therefore gets 2 personal credits although only one person files. Personal, blind and senior credits are not allowed to a filer someone else can claim as a dependent (PDF page 12).

Exemption credit AGI limitation (PDF page 14): over federal AGI of 252,203 (single, married/RDP filing separately), 504,411 (married/RDP filing jointly, qualifying surviving spouse/RDP) or 378,310 (head of household), each credit loses 6 for each 2,500 (1,250 if married/RDP filing separately) of excess or part of it; a 153 credit is gone 62,500 over the amount (31,250 if filing separately), a 475 credit 197,500 over (98,750). This is a stepped phase-down, but its step amounts are not printed, so it is recorded with effect 'other', the threshold and the worksheet in as_printed; no steps are listed.

Social Security: exempt. PDF page 60 Schedule CA line 6: 'California excludes U.S. social security benefits or equivalent Tier 1 railroad retirement benefits from taxable income'; checked against PDF page 67 (claim of right: 'Social security benefits are not taxable by California') and PDF page 13 line 14 ('differences between your federal and California income, e.g., social security benefits').

Railroad retirement: Tier 1 is excluded with Social Security (line 6) and benefits on federal Form RRB-1099-R included in federal income are entered in column B of line 5 (PDF page 60), so all railroad retirement benefits are excluded; one relief entry holds both tiers.

Government pensions of California, its localities and the federal government (civilian): no subtraction is printed. PDF page 60, Line 5a and 5b - Pensions and Annuities: 'Generally, no adjustments are made on this line. However, if you received Tier 2 railroad retirement benefits or partially taxable distributions from a pension plan, you may need to make the following adjustments.' The only pension adjustments printed are Tier 2 railroad, the three-year-rule annuity and the military retirement exclusion; a public pension is taxed as included in federal AGI.

Pensions from other states' governments, New York State in particular: not found in the booklet. The booklet prints no subtraction, no reciprocity rule and no mention of another state's or New York's pension; such a pension falls under the general line 5 statement ('Generally, no adjustments are made on this line') and is taxed as included in federal AGI. No public_pension_other_state entry is recorded.

Private pensions, IRA and employer-plan distributions, Roth conversions: no exclusion or subtraction printed. PDF page 59, Line 4a and 4b - IRA Distributions: 'Generally, no adjustments are made on this line. However, there may be significant differences in the taxable amount of a distribution (including a distribution from conversion of a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA), depending on when you made your contributions to the IRA.' Differences come from California basis (FTB Pub. 1005), not from an exclusion. PDF page 60 line 5 says the same for pensions and annuities. No age-based or retirement-income relief was found in the booklet.

Military Retirement Exclusion (PDF page 60 line 5; PDF pages 6 and 55 What's New): taxable years beginning on or after 2025-01-01 and before 2030-01-01; uniformed-services retirement pay or Department of Defense Survivor Benefit Plan annuity payments; up to 20,000 'for each type of payments'; capped at 20,000 for 'a surviving spouse, spouses filing a joint return, and any other individual'; federal AGI not over 125,000 (250,000 for 'a surviving spouse or spouses filing a joint return'). Read as a per-return cap of 20,000 and a 125,000 limit for every status except joint and surviving spouse. 'Surviving spouse' is read as the qualifying surviving spouse/RDP status (a judgement call); the booklet does not say what happens above the limit, and 'must not exceed' is read as no exclusion (effect removes). covers lists 'annuity' only for the Survivor Benefit Plan annuity (other_conditions).
Interest on U.S. obligations is subtracted in Schedule CA column B line 2 (PDF page 59), recorded as exempt_in_full of that interest.
Capital gains: PDF page 60 line 7a: 'California taxes long and short term capital gains as regular income. No special rate for long term capital gains exists.' capital_gains is empty.

Indexing: the booklet does not say whether the brackets, standard deduction, exemption credits, their AGI limits or the military exclusion limits are adjusted for inflation (searched: inflation, indexed, adjusted annually, cost of living). all_other not_stated.
Recapture: none printed. The exemption-credit AGI limitation reduces credits, not the lower brackets, so it is not recapture.

Not recorded (credits outside the record's scope, design.md): Senior Head of Household credit (PDF page 15, code 163: 65 or older, qualifying individual died in 2023 or 2024, AGI not over 98,652, 2% of taxable income up to 1,860), joint custody head of household and dependent parent credits, the nonrefundable renter's credit, the California earned income tax credit and the young child tax credit.

Page numbers: the booklet's printed page numbers equal the PDF page numbers (PDF page 75 is printed 'Page 75'), so every cite is a PDF page.

income_test.as_printed: Line 32 - Exemption Credits: 'Exemption credits reduce your tax. If your federal AGI on line 13 is more than the amount shown below for your filing status, your credits will be limited.' Single or married/RDP filing separately $252,203; married/RDP filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse/RDP $504,411; head of household $378,310. AGI Limitation Worksheet: c = line 13 less the amount; d = c divided by $2,500 ($1,250 if married/RDP filing separately), rounded to the next higher whole number; e = d x $6; the dollar amount of lines 7, 8 and 9 is reduced by e for each box (lines f to i) and the dollar amount of line 10 by e for each dependent (lines j to m), neither below zero. So each 153 or 475 credit loses 6 for each 2,500 (1,250) of AGI or part of it over the amount.
